Eduarda, let's be honest. We're in a deadlock. We offered eighty million, and your client wants a hundred.
I understand, Daniel. But eighty was an anchor, and we both know the business is worth more.
Maybe. But we have leverage. Your client needs to close before the debt matures.
True, but my client has a fallback option. Another buyer called us last week.
Okay. If we paid a hundred million upfront, our investment committee would never approve it.
Then let's look for a trade-off. What if part of the price were an earn-out?

Hi Eduarda, it's James. A few thoughts before your call with Northgate tomorrow. Don't accept their first number. Eighty million is only an anchor. Remember our leverage: we have a second buyer. If they offered ninety million upfront, I would take it to the client. If they stayed at eighty, I would walk away, but only after you test the earn-out. Make it clear that any earn-out is contingent on keeping the management team. And speak in hypotheticals: if you paid this, we would do that. It gives you room to move without making a firm promise. Call me after the meeting.

Here is a simple rule for any negotiation. Never give something without getting something back. That is a trade-off, and the grammar helps you make it. Use the second conditional to test an idea: if you extended the deadline, we would lower the price. It sounds like a question, not a commitment. When you are ready to commit, switch to the first conditional: if you sign this week, we will include the warranty. And when you need a firm condition, use provided that or as long as: we will agree, provided that the payment is made in cash. Finally, always know your fallback option before you sit down. Without it, you have no leverage.

Eduarda refused to accept the buyer's anchor of eighty million. She reminded Daniel that her client had a fallback option. She tested an idea: if part of the price were an earn-out, both sides would win. Daniel agreed, provided that the targets were realistic. They made the deal contingent on keeping the management team. Finally, they met halfway at ninety million upfront.
